_doc: Monotone ratchet for scripts/check-runbook-coverage.mjs (INV-148). `uncoveredOperational` is the number of tier-operational invariants that no runbook declares in its `handles:`. It is a DEBT COUNTER, not a rule: there are 49 operational invariants and two runbooks, and shipping "every operational invariant needs a runbook" as a hard rule would be red on arrival and instantly baselined into meaninglessness. As a ratchet the debt is visible, bounded, and cannot grow in silence. Unlike the ADR ratchet, --update-baseline RECORDS a rise rather than refusing it, because the counter is over a catalog this gate does not own and adding an operational invariant legitimately raises it (INV-08); what stays refused is a SILENT rise, since the new number lands in the diff either way.
_measured: 2026-09-05, wave 8: 49 of 49 operational invariants uncovered. Both existing runbooks handle non-operational invariants — RB-01 (dependabot triage) handles INV-74/76, both security; RB-02 (codex parity) handles INV-53/59. That 49/49 is the honest starting number and is exactly why this is a ratchet. The 10 operational invariants whose `enforcement` names no script at all are the honest first targets for burning it down, since those are the ones where a human procedure is the only enforcement there will ever be.
